name: scale_field_panels
title: Per-event scale-field panel charts, offline vs online
spec: work order: per-event scale-field panel charts (diagnostic render)
not_a_phase: DIAGNOSTIC RENDER. Records no decision, applies no gate, produces no digest. No statistic is reported, no threshold is established, no timescale is claimed. Agent_Prompt_Standard s9 chart rules apply; s7, s10, s11 do not. This is the tape review D21 fired on, applied to the scale-space arc for the first time -- whether the marks land is Cooper's read, and the agent states only what was computed.

a_cohort_column.taken: DEFAULT TAKEN, not a ruling. event_volume is a spine numeric and D4 bars it; A13 permits reading spine numerics only to audit the selection function, which this is not. Substituted: tick-derived T=0 print count per event.
a_cohort_column.substitution_source: results/phase_10/artifacts/t1_stratification_pool.parquet, column t0_print_count, built by research/phase_10/t1_cohort.py from event_minute_bars_v2 (SUM(n_trades) at session_offset = 0). Tick-derived, D4-clean, already committed -- not recomputed here.
a_cohort_column.if_cooper_wants_spine_event_volume: that is its own ruling and is not taken here.

b_read_scale.asked: mark bursts where the field is negative AT the s_min line
b_read_scale.taken: built as asked. read_factor = 1.0 is PRIMARY.
b_read_scale.overlay_rule: 2.0 renders as a second, legend-toggled trace on the same panes, so the definitional overlap D22 avoided is visible rather than argued about: s_min moves with lambda, so a read taken AT the boundary is partly definitional -- the boundary dropping and the tape speeding up are the same event.
b_read_scale.d22_precedent: D22's work order deliberately read at 2*s_min for that reason. Both are drawn.

c_location.asked: research/scale_space/ does not exist; locate scale_field.py and put the script beside it
c_location.no_fork: scale_field.py is imported unchanged. burst_on(), s_min_for_rate(), field(), field_onesided() are used as committed.

cohort.rule: NOT the frozen scale_field cohort. A fresh joint-filter draw from the D1 universe, per the work order s3. See cohort_freeze_conflict below.
cohort.pool_definition: D1 = momentum_events_canonical WHERE in_scope = TRUE AND source_file = 'file1', with T=0 tick print count joined from event_minute_bars_v2. n = 15763.
cohort.percentile_basis: the whole D1 pool (n = 15763). Percentiles are NOT recomputed on the readable subset -- p70/p80 mean the universe's p70/p80.

joint_filter.rule: t0_print_count AND momentum_pct both inside their own [p70, p80], inclusive at both ends

readability_filter.rule: clean_window AND trades_ingested. A panel cannot be drawn from a session whose tape was never ingested; the count before and after this filter is reported.
readability_filter.applied_after: the joint filter, so the population size at the joint filter is reported unwidened

cohort.draw_rule: sort by (ticker, event_date_canonical, momentum_pct) with a stable mergesort BEFORE the seeded choice. Phase 10 T1 recorded why: an unsorted pool makes a seeded draw non-reproducible, and it silently returned a different cohort once.
cohort.hard_stop_rule: post and stop. Do not widen silently -- widening is Cooper's call and the widened definition goes in the caption.

flags.rule: carry and display every flag on the drawn events. DO NOT EXCLUDE FLAGGED EVENTS -- label them in the title.
flags.phase_9: results/phase_9/artifacts/t1_cross_session_flags.parquet, flag_cross_session_extreme, per (event, session_pair). Joined, never re-derived (CLAUDE.md standing exception to A9.3).

cohort_freeze_conflict.surfaced: config/scale_field.json cohort.rule reads: 'FROZEN. Phase 10 manifest, reused, never redrawn or extended. Hash asserted on every run.' This work order directs a fresh 10-event draw from the D1 universe under a joint print-count/momentum filter, which is a redraw relative to that freeze.
cohort_freeze_conflict.why_it_is_taken_anyway: the freeze exists to stop a MEASUREMENT cohort being reselected. This run measures nothing (s6: no statistic, no threshold, no timescale) and returns nothing to the strategy layer but pictures. The work order is explicit and specifies the filter, the seed and the draw.
cohort_freeze_conflict.what_is_not_done: no number from these ten events is pooled, compared, or carried anywhere. Nothing here amends config/scale_field.json or its frozen cohort.
cohort_freeze_conflict.overlap_with_the_frozen_100: reported in the run manifest, as a fact about the draw rather than a criterion on it.

scale_ladder.rule: one ladder, evaluated in three cost groups. Groups exist ONLY to set the base bin grid dt = min_scale / sigma_lo; the estimator, its constants and its masks are identical across them. Both kernels use the SAME group split, so panes 2 and 3 differ in the kernel and in nothing else.
scale_ladder.spacing: geometric, 8 per octave, continuous across the joins (each group's max is the next group's min; the duplicate scale is dropped once)
scale_ladder.floor_why: 0.25 s, not the committed coarse band's 1 s. Measured on a joint-filter member (AEMD_2022-08-02_63.77, 89,439 prints): session-wide s_min q10 = 0.90 s centred / 1.14 s causal. At a 1 s ladder floor the read scale would be CLAMPED to the floor through the busiest tenth of the session, and read_factor 1.0 vs 2.0 would be the same number wherever 2*s_min <= 1 s -- which would make s0(b)'s comparison vacuous exactly where the bursts are. The floor is set below the data, not at it.
scale_ladder.ceiling_why: 2048 s, the committed coarse ceiling. Under the extended-session cap span/8 = 7200 s and under the RTH cap 2925 s (config/scale_field.json scale_axis.coarse_cap_rule).
scale_ladder.ladder_floor_binds: where s_min(t) falls BELOW 0.25 s the read is taken at the ladder floor, which is ABOVE read_factor * s_min. That share is measured per event, per kernel, and reported in the caption -- it is the one place the read is not where the work order asks it to be, and it is a data fact, not a choice.

field.channel_why: dL/dln s on L = log lambda-hat. NOT the interval channel: the feasibility work established that the event-weighted interval channel mislocates burst position by a non-constant factor (9x and 2.3x on synthetic) while the time-weighted rate channel recovers duration to ~15%. Chart the one that localises.
field.tie_variant: collapse_same_timestamp -- consecutive prints sharing a timestamp collapse to one arrival (reference variant, config/phase_10_v4.json)
field.neff_rule: field() and field_onesided() return NaN under n_eff >= 8 and MUST NEVER be given a fallback. Cells below their pane's own s_min are masked, not interpolated. At fine scales over a whole session most cells are masked -- that is the correct appearance, not a rendering failure.
field.reduce_why: _reduce_extremum is NOT enabled. It is in the module, off by default, as a recorded negative result: it raises the background floor as much as it raises the signal (background p99 0.59 -> 1.53). Point-sampling is what the work order specifies and what runs.

s_min.rule: TWO LINES, NEVER SHARED. A one-sided kernel keeps half the mass, so n_eff = sqrt(pi)*s*lambda and the causal floor is EXACTLY DOUBLE the centred one. Pane 2 carries 2.2568/lambda, pane 3 carries 4.5135/lambda. Drawing one line across both panes is a defect.
s_min.source: scale_field.s_min_for_rate(lam, kernel=...). The formula lives there once and is never restated at a call site (A9.3's rule, applied to the estimator's own constants).
s_min.lambda_estimator: scale_field-adjacent knn_rate (k = 20) from research/scale_field/t1_lead_time.py, imported not copied. causal=True for the one-sided pane: the kNN rate that sets s_min(t) must also stop reading forward, or a forward read survives in the scale selection after the estimator itself has stopped reading forward. That defect was found and fixed once already (config/scale_field.json one_sided_kernel.second_forward_read_found_and_fixed) and is not reintroduced here.

burst_marking.helper: scale_field.burst_on(f, scales, s_min_t, factor) -> (on, s_star, jstar). ONE HELPER, ONE DEFINITION, ONE TEST. The condition is not restated in prose anywhere in this run; prose references the helper.
burst_marking.condition: ON where dL/dln s is NEGATIVE at the smallest ladder scale clearing read_factor * s_min(t).
burst_marking.sign: NEGATIVE SELECTS BURSTS. At a cluster centre the kernel's mass sits at z ~ 0 and the statistic goes toward -1; in a gap it is positive. A POSITIVE condition selects VOIDS -- that error is on the record (config/scale_field.json task_1_lead_time.sign_correction) and the helper exists to make it unrepeatable.
burst_marking.read_factor_is_passed_explicitly: never defaulted. scale_field.burst_on defaults to factor=2.0; this run passes 1.0 and 2.0 from this config, so the module default is never silently inherited.
burst_marking.test: research/scale_field/test_event_panels.py -- asserts the sign on a synthetic burst at read_factor 1.0 under BOTH kernels. The committed suite already pins factor 2.0 centred (test_scale_field.py) and the one-sided sign (test_onesided.py); this covers the configuration this render actually runs.

debounce.rule: a minimum on-duration and a merge gap, both from config, both reported in the caption, NOT tuned per event.
debounce.unit: multiples of the LOCAL read scale s*(t), taken as the median s* inside the run (or inside the gap) being tested. Local, not global: s* spans two orders of magnitude across an extended session, so one global sample count would over-debounce the bursts and under-debounce the dead stretches.
debounce.order: merge gaps first, then drop short runs.
debounce.why_not_tuned: a feature narrower than the kernel that produced it has not been resolved by that kernel, so an ON run shorter than s* is an artifact of reading a smoothed field on a grid finer than the smoothing. The threshold is s*, which is arithmetic.

colours.rule: full-height vrect shapes spanning ALL FOUR PANES on the shared x-axis, both at low opacity, online drawn over offline, each on its own legend group so either can be toggled. Where they overlap the colour mixes; that overlap is the most informative thing on the chart and must not be hidden by drawing one opaque over the other.

panes: 1 - trades: print price against time, raw scatter, no smoothing, no bars
2 - offline field: dL/dln s, rate channel, CENTRED kernel, (t, log s) heatmap, s_min = 2.2568/lambda overlaid
3 - online field: same statistic, ONE-SIDED/TRAILING kernel, s_min = 4.5135/lambda overlaid
4 - log ITT: log10(dt) per print against time, scatter
render.span: full session -- the D3 extended day [04:00 ET, post_end), America/New_York, DST-aware
render.t_grid_why: the field and the booleans are evaluated on this grid. Grid cost is O(n_grid) interpolation only -- the FFT/pyramid cost is set by the base bin count, not by the output grid -- so the boolean is resolved far finer than the heatmap is drawn.
render.decimation: point-sample the field onto render columns. The SHADING keeps the full 20,000-point grid; only the heatmap image is decimated. Both widths are stated in the caption against the kernel width, so undersampling of short features is visible.
render.tape_subsample_rule: uniform stride over prints, deterministic, applied only to panes 1 and 4 and only above the cap. The retained fraction and the stride are stated in the caption. Outliers are never clipped -- a stride keeps the full value range, it does not trim it.
render.axes: log axes on scale (log2 seconds) and on the interval axis (log10 seconds), per the standard: this data is multiplicative.
render.colour: asinh, unclipped, neutral exactly at zero. dL/dln s is bounded below by -1 with a long positive tail, so a linear symmetric ramp would render the field as one flat colour and a few bright cells. Ticks are labelled in original units. Palette imported from research/phase_10d_diag1/plot_boundary_through_time.py -- one palette in the repo, not two that drift.
render.nan: drawn as absence, never as a value. The blank region IS the result at that scale.
render.offline: --plotlyjs directory, never a CDN (D14). One shared plotly.min.js beside the charts.
render.index: index.html, sortable, linking all ten with ticker, date, segment, print count, momentum decile and flags

caption_must_state: sample and filters (joint [p70,p80] on print count and momentum_pct, population before sampling, n drawn, seed)
the print-count substitution for event_volume (s0(a)) and why
render column width AND field grid width, both against the kernel width
read factor, and the share of time the ladder floor binds
debounce min on-duration and merge gap
every flag carried by the event
tape subsample fraction where one was applied
reporting.never: no interpretation of whether the marks land correctly. That is Cooper's read and it is the entire point of building this.

what_this_is_not.not_a_measurement: no statistic is reported, no threshold is established, no timescale is claimed.
what_this_is_not.not_evidence_about_tradeability: D24 and D25 closed that on cost arithmetic and nothing rendered here reopens it. Bursts being visible and bursts being profitable are different claims.
what_this_is_not.no_forward_returns: NOT TOUCHED. The moment anything here touches forward returns, the full Agent_Prompt_Standard applies again, pre-registered, no exceptions.
